% ---------------------------------------------------------------- I.1
\begin{finding}{major}{f:opening-extra-sumcheck}{The opening phase runs a sumcheck leanVM does not run}
\fhead{Evidence} \Cref{sec:gen-opening-after-lambda,sec:gen-opening-blueprint} (\code{08:99};
\code{stack_open.rs:452-461}; \code{whir.rs:1324-1334}; \code{py:1362, 1012}).

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint, caused by the evaluation interface of Layer 0.

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{Layer 10 (\code{bp:1112-1114}), with the convention \emph{The oracle} and Layers 0, 11 and 12}
\asis
\begin{leancode}
def openingPhase (μ) (J : ℕ) : OracleReduction []ₒ (StmtIn := Fin J → WeightedClaim μ) … (StmtOut := Unit) …
    (pSpec := V_to_P : E ; sumcheck (W_λ · q) rounds ; the final evaluation query)
theorem openingPhase_rbrKnowledgeSoundness : … ((J − 1)/|E| on λ, 2/|E| per round)
\end{leancode}
\asproposed
\begin{leancode}
def openingPhase (I) : Phase.Def I (I.Stmt × FlockOut I) Unit
    (pSpec := V_to_P : E)   -- λ; the verifier queries the stack once, at W_λ, and compares with C_λ
theorem openingPhase_rbrKnowledgeSoundness : … ((J − 1)/|E| on λ)   -- the batching component G3
\end{leancode}
with, in the convention \emph{The oracle} (\code{bp:317}), ``\code{OracleInterface} query
\code{Vector E μ_stack} and answer \code{eval₂Mle q}'' replaced by ``\code{OracleInterface} query
\code{Weight μ_stack} (specification Definition 3.13) and answer $Σ_w W(w)·q(w)$; an evaluation is the
query \code{eqWeight r}''; in Layer 0 (\code{bp:637-642}) the instance accordingly, \lean{Weight}
moved below it; in Layer 11 the sentence ``its level-0 batching challenge is the opening phase's
$λ$: the compilation replaces the opening phase by \lean{whirOpen}''; in Layer 12 (\code{bp:1214})
``WHIR in place of the evaluation oracle'' $→$ ``WHIR in place of the opening phase, over the
level-0 word as the commit message''; the title of Layer 10 and \code{bp:127} lose ``the opening
sumcheck''.
\reason The deployed transcript after $λ$ is WHIR's, whose sumcheck is interleaved with its
commitments and closes on one equation; the sketched transcript has $μ$ extra rounds and an extra
scalar, so \lean{verify_iff_compiled} cannot hold for Rust proofs. The alternative (iii) of
\cref{sec:gen-opening-alternatives} is acceptable; (i) is not.
\end{change}
\end{finding}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- I.2
\begin{finding}{major}{f:opening-verify-iff-compiled}{\texttt{verify\_iff\_compiled} names definitions that do not describe the compiled verifier}
\fhead{Evidence} \Cref{sec:gen-opening-iff-compiled} (the probe of \cref{sec:gen-opening-probe-fs};
\code{Basic.lean:490-496}, \code{FiatShamir/Basic.lean:129-136}, \code{BCS/Basic.lean:59-63} at
\code{dca90385}; \code{fs/transcript.rs:9-12, 223-224}, the citation check correcting the
dossier's \code{:225-228}; \code{fs/lib.rs:165-174}).

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint; the absence of a BCS transform in ArkLib is a
deviation forced upstream (issue \#627 has no implementation and excludes ROM soundness).

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{\lean{verify_iff_compiled} (\code{bp:1218-1221, 1231-1232})}
\asis The theorem with \code{Verifier.fiatShamir (leanVmIopp …).verifier} and ``\code{decode s proof}'',
``unconditional: it is about two definitions''.
\asproposed The statement of \cref{sec:gen-opening-iff-compiled},
\begin{leancode}
theorem verify_iff_compiled (prog input proof) :
    verify prog input proof = true ↔
      ∃ s, s.Admissible prog ∧ ∃ msgs, decode prog s proof = some msgs ∧
        runWithChain (bcsCompile (leanVmIopp prog s)).verifier (blake2sChain prog s) input msgs
          = some () ∧ grindingChecks prog s msgs = true
\end{leancode}
with \lean{bcsCompile} (a leanerVM definition, Layer 12: oracle messages replaced by roots, the
openings as messages of the last round or as an appended message, the verifier's queries answered
from authenticated rows), \code{blake2sChain prog s} (the chain as a \lean{QueryImpl}), and
\lean{grindingChecks} conjoined; and the sentence ``unconditional, about two definitions,
\textbf{and} a check only because \lean{verify} is written from §8.5 before the right-hand side is
unfolded''.
\end{change}
\end{finding}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- I.3
\begin{finding}{major}{f:opening-not-probability}{\texttt{baseVerifier\_extractsExecution} and \texttt{verify\_knowledgeSound} are not probability statements}
\fhead{Evidence} \Cref{sec:gen-opening-extracts} (\code{bp:1247-1248}, \code{bp:326};
\code{architecture.md:264-273}). The citation check adds that the Merkle leaf hash is multi-block
BLAKE2s-256, not the one 64-byte compression, so the random oracle of the proposed statements must
cover it separately or through the iterated construction.

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint (and of \file{docs/architecture.md}'s target
theorem, base proof extraction and completeness (T4), which it transcribes).

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{\lean{baseVerifier_extractsExecution} (\code{bp:1247-1248}), \lean{verify_knowledgeSound}, and the base theorem (T4) in \code{architecture.md:264-269}}
\asis
\begin{leancode}
theorem baseVerifier_extractsExecution (fs bcs mca flock) (h : verify prog input proof = true) :
    except with probability niError, ∃ t, ValidExecution prog input t
\end{leancode}
\asproposed The two statements of \cref{sec:gen-opening-extracts}: a random oracle $H$ for the
compression function, a $Q$-query adversary $A^H$ outputting \code{(prog, input, proof)} with its
query log, the straight-line extractor \lean{extract} (leaves off the log, list decoding,
selection), the event ``$\mathit{verify}^H$ accepts and \code{witnessOf (extract …)} fails
\lean{SatisfiedBy}'' of probability $≤ \mathit{niError}\ Q$, and the existential corollary; the
sentence ``the random-oracle heuristic, that BLAKE2s's compression function instantiates $H$, is the
one non-formal step, named here and in \code{architecture.md}''; and in
\code{architecture.md:264-269} the same repair of the base theorem (T4).
\reason For fixed \code{(prog, input, proof)} the hypothesis is decidable and the conclusion is a
fixed proposition; the only randomness is the oracle's, and the only knowledge statement is about
an extractor.
\end{change}
\end{finding}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- I.4
\begin{finding}{major}{f:opening-fs-bcs-interfaces}{The Fiat--Shamir and BCS interfaces cannot be inhabited, and one is false as stated}
\fhead{Evidence} \Cref{sec:gen-opening-interfaces} (\code{FiatShamir/Basic.lean:163-175},
\code{Security/Implications.lean:230-254, 305-313}, \code{BCS/Basic.lean},
\code{Commitments/Functional/Basic.lean:250-255} at \code{dca90385}, the same text at \code{7653a901}
at \code{Security/Implications.lean:200-224, 275-283} and \code{Commitments/Functional/Basic.lean:249-254}
as the citation check found; pull request \#848's
\file{SingleSalt.lean:973-993}; issue \#627's plan; \file{literature.md}, section A.3). The citation check adds, for the proposed
\lean{BcsSecurity}: the Merkle leaves are BLAKE2s-256 of 512 or 384 bytes, eight or six chained
compressions, so a random oracle for the one 64-byte compression does not cover them; the interface
must model the leaf hash by a second oracle or through the iterated construction.

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint (the universal claim of the comment is false; \#627
is not a pull request); the missing upstream theorems are a deviation forced by ArkLib, whose
workaround is to name the literature and the construction.

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{the assumed interfaces (\code{bp:1223-1225}), \lean{verify_knowledgeSound}, the ledger row on Fiat--Shamir and BCS security (A5, \code{bp:263}) and the holes table (\code{bp:614})}
\asis
\begin{leancode}
/-- Assumed interfaces, each an ArkLib theorem to come (ledger A5). -/
structure FiatShamirSecurity where …   -- rbr knowledge soundness of the IOPP ⇒ knowledge soundness of its FS compilation in the ROM, error Q · max_i ε_i
structure BcsSecurity where …          -- Merkle-compiled oracles: extraction from collision resistance / ROM
\end{leancode}
\asproposed
\begin{leancode}
/-- Assumed interfaces. No theorem of ArkLib states them at either pin (its Fiat–Shamir completeness is admitted for a constant oracle, its BCS transform is commented out, its round-by-round ⇒ state-restoration implication is commented out); their witness obligation is the literature (BCS16, CY24 Thm 25.2.1/31.2.1, BGKTTZ23 Thm 3.15) for the parts it covers, and a new statement for grinding. -/
structure RbrToStateRestoration where …  -- worst-case rbr knowledge soundness ⇒ state-restoration knowledge soundness at (Q + rounds)·max_i ε_i
structure BcsSecurity where …            -- the IOP of E.3, Merkle-compiled with H random, keeps state-restoration knowledge soundness up to 3(Q² + 1)/2^256, with the straight-line extractor reading leaves off the query log; hypothesis: leaf width and height fixed by the verifier
structure ChainFiatShamirSecurity where … -- the hash chain of fs/lib.rs with H random, with proof-of-work rounds of b_i bits, turns state-restoration knowledge soundness ε_sr(Q) into adaptive knowledge soundness ε_sr(Q) + c·Q²/2^256, a query at a ground round costing 2^{b_i} queries of H
\end{leancode}
(``the IOP of E.3'' is the composed IOP of \cref{sec:gen-opening-listbinding}), and
\code{verify_knowledgeSound (rs : RbrToStateRestoration) (bcs) (fs : ChainFiatShamirSecurity) (mca : McaJohnson) (lc : ListCompile) (flock)}.
In the ledger row on Fiat--Shamir and BCS security (A5, \code{bp:263}) and the holes table (\code{bp:614}): ``\#848 and \#469
(single-salt and duplex-sponge Fiat--Shamir from state-restoration soundness, ideal per-round
oracle, no proof of work); \#627 is a design issue for the BCS transform whose plan excludes ROM
soundness''.
\reason An interface quantified over all IOPPs with error $Q·\max ε_i$ is false (hash term, oracle
messages, grinding), and a hypothesis that is false makes the theorem vacuous.
\end{change}
\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{major}{f:opening-list-binding}{The list-binding compilation is a theorem the blueprint names and does not state}
\fhead{Evidence} \Cref{sec:gen-opening-listbinding,sec:gen-opening-hidden} (\code{B:4, 70-72,
133-137}; \code{whir_config.rs:593-599}; \code{bp:1190, 1296-1299};
\cref{f:flock-ring-list-size}; \file{literature.md}, section A.3, item 4, and section G.2).

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint (omission).

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{Layer 12 (\code{bp:1190}) and \lean{niError}}
\asis ``Layer 12 turns list binding into extraction of the one $q$ that satisfies every pooled
claim.''
\asproposed In Layer 12, the theorem of \cref{sec:gen-opening-listbinding} (the list-binding
compilation) with its extractor (list-decode, select), its state function, its errors ($L_0·ε_i$ at
the front's challenges, Theorem B.7's at WHIR's), and its two lemmas: every member of $Λ(w)$ is

\begin{finding}{major}{f:opening-completeness-grinding}{Perfect completeness does not survive the transform}
\fhead{Evidence} \Cref{sec:gen-opening-completeness} (\code{fs/lib.rs:126-155};
\code{Compose.lean:94-104}; \cref{f:flock-ring-test20-completeness,f:flock-ring-rust-prover-incomplete};
\file{lib-arklib.md}, section G.2).

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint.

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{the proof sketch of the target theorem (\code{bp:1255-1257})}
\asis ``the second composes \lean{constraintCompleteness}, \lean{m3Holds_stackOf},
\lean{piop_perfectCompleteness} and the determinism of the Fiat--Shamir chain (perfect completeness
survives the transform without any assumption).''
\asproposed ``the second composes \lean{constraintCompleteness}, \lean{m3Holds_stackOf},
\lean{piop_perfectCompleteness} and the determinism of the chain: an honest interactive proof on
the chain's challenges is the compiled proof (an equation between definitions). The grinding is a
search (\code{fs/lib.rs:126-155}); \lean{prove} takes fuel and returns \code{Option Proof}, and
\lean{baseProver_complete} is \code{prove … = some proof → verify … proof = true}.''
\reason No theorem gives the honest prover a nonce.
\end{change}
\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{major}{f:opening-nierror}{\texttt{niError} cannot carry leanVM's 128-bit claim}
\fhead{Evidence} \Cref{sec:gen-opening-deployed-claim,sec:gen-opening-nierror}
(\code{whir_config.rs:25-27, 36-38, 57-60, 537-568, 593-599}; \code{leaf.rs:108-118}; the scratch port
of \cref{sec:gen-opening-probe-params}; \file{literature.md}, section A.3).

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint.

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{\lean{niError} (\code{bp:1234-1235}) and acceptance test 23}
\asis ``\lean{niError} is the round-by-round maximum times the query bound plus the
grinding-adjusted WHIR terms.''
\asproposed ``\code{niError Q} is $(Q + \mathit{rounds})$ times the largest per-challenge error of
the compiled protocol ($L_0·ε_i$ at each oracle-protocol challenge, Theorem B.7's fold, OOD and
batching terms, and $2^{−17}·(1 − γ_i)^{t_i}$ at each ground query round) plus the hash term
$c·Q^2/2^{256}$; at the deployed parameters the maximum is the query rounds' $2^{−128}$ and the fold
rounds' $2^{−128.2}$, in the Johnson regime conditional on Theorem 4.6, for every admissible
$(μ, ρ)$ (the query counts of \code{py:910}).'' And in acceptance test 23: ``$Σ\,\mathit{piopError} <
2^{-150}$ is the interactive error of the oracle protocol at admissible sizes (below $2^{-159}$ with
the window); it is not the security level of \lean{verify}, which the WHIR query rounds set at 128
bits including 17 bits of grinding.''
\reason \Cref{sec:gen-opening-numbers}.
\end{change}
\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{minor}{f:opening-chain-step}{The chain's step is the 64-byte hash, not the compression with the state as chaining value}
\fhead{Evidence} \Cref{sec:gen-opening-chain} (\code{fs/lib.rs:18-24};
\code{primitives/src/hash.rs:83-87, 209-224}; \code{bp:216, 325, 1204}). The citation check agrees
that the chain state fills the first eight message words of BLAKE2s's $F$, whose $h$ input is always
\code{PARAM_IV}, and adds two qualifications: \code{bp:216} also calls the byte hasher ``the RFC 7693
wrapper over \code{compress} with the last-block flag only'', so the blueprint's reading is an
inference; and the Lean rendering the dossier proposes in \cref{sec:gen-opening-chain} must use
leanISA's signature, \code{UInt32} flags and the parameter-folded IV
(\code{primitives/src/hash.rs:64-81}).

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{the \emph{Fiat--Shamir} row of the conventions (\code{bp:325})}
\asproposed ``every step is $\text{BLAKE2s-256}(\mathit{cv} ‖ \mathit{block})$ over 64 bytes, that
is the RFC compression $F(\mathit{paramIV}, \mathit{cv} ‖ \mathit{block}, t = 64, f_0 = 1)$ with the
chain state in the message; \lean{compress} of leanISA Layer 1 is $F$''.
\reason The two readings are different functions; transcribed content (the blueprint's
Category B).
\end{change}
\end{finding}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- I.16
\begin{finding}{minor}{f:opening-status-python-caps}{The status file's finding on the Python verifier's caps is false at the pin}

\fhead{Evidence} \code{py:856-864} at \code{a386121f} checks $16 ≤ \mathit{log\_memory} ≤ 32$,
